title: Catalyst Therapeutics — Ramp to Prod: Playbook & Handoff
header:
Date: 2026-12-27
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~44 minutes
Recording: Fireflies auto transcript
Location: Zoom
Notes: onboarding/ramp-to-production planning call; AE+SE+CSM from Redwood; security and infra stakeholders from Catalyst
summary: Kickoff for production ramp with focus on deployment mode (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), SSO/KMS requirements, runbook ownership, and pilot success criteria. Agreed to baseline performance benchmark, security docs to be shared, and a short pilot on Dedicated with fallbacks to hosted. Next steps include schedule for bench run, security questionnaire answers, and a one-week exec sync.
topics: Security controls: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
action_items: Priya (Redwood SE) to run a 2-hour benchmark with Catalyst test corpus next Tue and share token/latency spreadsheet
Alex (AE) to send Dedicated sizing worksheet and preliminary pricing estimate by EOD Friday
Lina (Catalyst Sec) to send completed security questionnaire and a list of additional compliance docs requested within 3 business days
Jorge (CSM) to draft the onboarding runbook outline and share for review by next Wednesday
David (Catalyst Eng) to provision a VPC peering test account creds for Private eval if needed (optional)
next_steps: Schedule benchmark slot (Priya/Catalyst) — target next Tue 09:00 PT
Send Dedicated sizing + pricing (Alex) — target Friday EOD
Security questionnaire and addl docs (Catalyst) — within 3 business days
Follow-up exec sync (30 min) after benchmark — tentatively Dec 31
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mills: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, we'll run through the ramp playbook and then go into the security questions.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Hi all, Maya here.
[00:11] David Park: David, platform.
[00:13] Lina Torres: Lina from security.
[00:15] Tom Greer: Tom here for product.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya from Redwood SE. Jorge on mute until later.
[00:22] Jorge Alvarez: (joins) Sorry, late train, Jorge CSM.
[00:26] Alex Mills: Cool, quick agenda, 1) current infra and constraints, 2) deployment recommendation, 3) bench and SLOs, 4) security/compliance items, 5) runbook and owners, 6) next steps.
[00:40] Tom Greer: For context, we're doing clinical data extraction and triage for trials — latency matters but cost is also a big constraint. SLO is sub-350 ms p50 for short prompts, p95 under 700, throughput about 25 qps steady.
[01:02] Priya Nair: Got it. That maps to what we typically see. quick question, are you planning to persist any PHI or are you tokenizing at the edge?
[01:10] Maya Chen: We separate PHI out, so the payloads that hit models are pseudo-anon but they do include structured identifiers occasionally. We need audit logs and strict retention.
[01:20] Lina Torres: And we need to ensure KMS integration for key lifecycle and we have to map to our existing HSM provider. SOC2 is table stakes and we'll need ISO docs if possible.
[01:32] Alex Mills: Understood. From a deployment standpoint, given the SLOs and audit needs, our recommendation is Dedicated for the pilot — predictable throughput and isolation. But we can start with Hosted to iterate quickly on prompts if you want faster time to value.
[01:50] David Park: Curious on the tradeoffs — Dedicated costs more but is there a big perf delta?
[01:57] Priya Nair: Performance delta is mostly about consistent tail latencies and isolation from noisy neighbors. Also Dedicated lets you pin instance/quantization profiles and eliminates cold-start noise. For 25 qps with those p95 goals we'd recommend an NVLink-backed pool with 2-3 nodes for headroom.
[02:18] Tom Greer: If we go Dedicated can we still use streaming and function-calls?
[02:22] Priya Nair: Yes, same API surface. A common confusion is thinking Dedicated changes the API — it doesn't. You get the same endpoints, same SDK behavior, just the underlying capacity is reserved.
[02:33] Lina Torres: On encryption, our HSM team will want KMS integration and customer-managed keys. Do you support external key wraps or only Redwood KMS?
[02:42] Alex Mills: We support customer-managed KMS on Private and Dedicated; hosted supports Redwood-managed keys but we do offer Bring-Your-Own-Key options for enterprise plans. I'll share the KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:54] Maya Chen: What about data residency? Some of our EU clinical partners can't have data cross borders.
[02:59] Priya Nair: We can pin requests to region and have data residency controls for Private/Dedicated deployments. For Hosted you can pick region but there are limits depending on model availability. We'll flag any model that isn't region-enabled.
[03:16] David Park: The other thing is runbook and oncall. Who owns the first-level oncall for inference failures?
[03:22] Jorge Alvarez: From CSM perspective we recommend a three-layer model: 1) App team monitors model errors + retries, 2) Redwood support for platform incidents (we provide tracing hooks and runbooks), 3) Escalation to eng if it's model regression. We'll include this in the onboarding runbook.
[03:40] Tom Greer: Ok, success criteria for the pilot — what's minimal?
[03:44] Alex Mills: Suggested pilot success: 1) Meet latency SLOs for targeted prompt set in two out of three runs, 2) No data exfiltration, keys verified with KMS, 3) Integration of audit logs into your SIEM, 4) Ops runbook and blameless run completed.
[03:58] Priya Nair: For the latency bench we'll need a representative corpus and traffic shape — bursty vs steady. Maya, can you share a scrubbed test corpus?
[04:06] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll provide an anonymized set this afternoon.
[04:10] Lina Torres: Also include the exact retention policy you want — we have to map that to Redwood's log retention.
[04:15] Alex Mills: Redwood supports configurable retention for logs and KV cache persistence can be tuned. Quick note: some customers refer to KV cache as 'KV cash' in tickets, haha.
[04:23] (laughter)
[04:25] David Park: We've got an internal RL policy that occasionally kills long-running tokens — will tokenization affect the KV cache behavior?
[04:33] Priya Nair: The KV cache is per-session and managed by the runtime. If you have TTLs or pruning policies client-side, we can align them. We'll document the behavior — it's in the ops guide.
[04:44] Tom Greer: Security doc request: Lina wants audit log format and sample event payloads.
[04:49] Alex Mills: We'll attach the sample logs and the schema. Also we'll include the SOC2 and ISO cert summaries and the shared responsibility matrix.
[04:57] Lina Torres: Great. Also, SSO integration — we use Okta with SAML. How mature is the console SAML support?
[05:04] Jorge Alvarez: Console SSO via SAML is supported with SCIM provisioning for users, roles, and RBAC. We can help set up the initial mappings during onboarding.
[05:13] Maya Chen: On pricing — if we start Hosted and then move to Dedicated, how does the billing transition work?
[05:19] Alex Mills: We bill Hosted usage per token until you provision Dedicated capacity. If you commit to a Dedicated reserved pool we can apply credits or convert a portion of prior usage in negotiation. Alex: I'll put a preliminary estimate into your CRM and send over a worksheet.
[05:33] Tom Greer: Any gotchas with model versioning during rollouts? We need stable outputs for compliance review.
[05:38] Priya Nair: We have model pinning and rollout controls: canary, A/B, automatic fallback. We also track evals — you can tie regressions to prompt sets and trigger alerts. For compliance, exportable eval reports are available.
[05:52] Lina Torres: Can Redwood produce an audit trail showing which model version generated a specific response?
[05:57] Priya Nair: Yes, request metadata includes model ID and runtime fingerprint. Those are emitted in logs which you can ship to your SIEM.
[06:07] David Park: About private deployments — if we wanted an on-prem box for certain partners, how fast is that path?
[06:13] Alex Mills: Private on-prem is more involved — we have a packaged offering but it needs network prep, KMS/HSM mapping, and an initial integration sprint. Typical lead time is 6–10 weeks. For quick wins, Dedicated is faster.
[06:26] Tom Greer: Timeline for pilot? We have Q1 milestones.
[06:30] Alex Mills: Proposed: bench next Tue, then a 2-week pilot on Dedicated (can be scaled up), and an exec checkpoint after the bench. If that goes well, production roll by mid-Jan.
[06:42] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. Lina, any blocking items?
[06:46] Lina Torres: As long as Redwood provides the KMS integration details and SOC2 artifacts quickly, we can unblock. Also we need confirmation on log retention options.
[06:55] Priya Nair: We'll email the KMS spec and SOC2 summary today and include examples of retention toggles.
[07:02] Alex Mills: Ok let's talk specifics: Priya will run the bench, she'll need an ingress endpoint and creds — David, can you stand up a small test account or give us a short-lived API key?
[07:12] David Park: We can create a service account and rotate keys. We'll aim to have that by Monday EOD.
[07:18] Jorge Alvarez: I'll draft the onboarding runbook: sections will be preflight checklist, security controls, bench instructions, rollback procedure, escalation matrix.
[07:27] Tom Greer: For alerting, we want PagerDuty integration. Is that in the console?
[07:31] Jorge Alvarez: Yes, we ship alerts to PagerDuty, Slack, and webhook endpoints. We'll show the alert mapping in the runbook.
[07:38] Maya Chen: Any competitors we should be aware of? We looked at MajorCloud-Endpoints but they didn't have the same on-prem flexibility, and Anthropic was cost-prohibitive for our volume.
[07:50] Alex Mills: Noted. Any other questions?
[07:53] Lina Torres: One last compliance ask — can we get a whitebox view of patching cadence for the runtime nodes?
[07:59] Priya Nair: We can provide patch cadence docs and change windows. For Dedicated we also allow maintenance windows aligned to your off-peak times.
[08:09] Tom Greer: Great. Let's recap the next steps.
[08:12] Alex Mills: Recap: Priya runs bench Tue, Alex sends Dedicated sizing and pricing by Friday, Catalyst provides anonymized corpus today and security questionnaire in 3 business days, Jorge drafts runbook by Wed, follow-up exec sync after bench.
[08:31] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone.
[08:33] David Park: Thanks.
[08:34] Lina Torres: Appreciate it.
[08:35] Jorge Alvarez: Thanks, I'll circulate the runbook outline.
